name: The Lounge Brawl
type: Intra-Party Skirmish / Document Retrieval / Debt-Motivated Theft
result: Tactical Draw — Papers recovered and returned to Saedia. Debt unresolved. Floor cracked. Waluigi on the floor. Wario at his next appointment.

attackers.name: Waluigi and Wario (Briefly, Opportunistically, and Without Prior Coordination)

defenders.name: The Party — Hjumpik, Toad Lee, Rakasha Azure, Stucky

casualties.attackers: Waluigi — axe to the legs, collision damage, fire from his own weapon, debt still outstanding, both kidneys still attached, cried on the floor. Wario — caught in Rakasha's iron grip briefly, ate papers, walked away entirely untroubled.
casualties.defenders: Hjumpik — took shuttlecock fire when Waluigi ran into him, described it afterward as 'alright, you hit me with it,' applied mushroom, recovered. Toad Lee — received Stucky's thrown eye on his head, exact expression unrecorded. Stucky — almost fell during ground pound, was helped up by Rakasha, eye recovered. Lounge floor — cracked. Structurally compromised. Ferngrove's maintenance staff has not been informed.

summary: At five in the morning, following hours of operational activity in the Feywild, Waluigi saw a window — Wario fell, papers uncontrolled, everyone's attention distributed across the collision — and went through it. He fired the Phase Spider gut racket, grabbed what he believed to be the papers, said 'I need it please,' and ran. The shuttlecock caught fire. He ran into Hjumpik. The fire damaged Hjumpik. Toad Lee pursued with an axe. Stucky threw her eye and missed. Wario ground-pounded the floor and cracked it. Rakasha caught Wario. Hjumpik deployed anchor skills and stopped. A third-party handoff through Rakasha was arranged. Wario ate papers in a moment only Waluigi witnessed. The real papers returned to Saedia. The debt is unresolved. Waluigi cried on the floor. Wario had clients to see.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this battle and Waluigi is aware that he lost it. Not militarily — the papers changed hands twice and ended up where they started, which is not a clean loss for either side. But in every other sense: Waluigi fired first, damaged an ally, was caught, sat on the floor, and watched Wario walk away. Waluigi has documented other people's tactical failures with considerable precision. He owes the same precision to his own.

**Prelude: The Window Opens**

The strategic context of the brawl is inseparable from what preceded it. Wario had offered to release Waluigi's entire debt — not reduce, release — in exchange for the aged papers. Hjumpik had refused on principle. Waluigi had proposed making a copy, which would have cost nothing except the time to make it. Hjumpik had refused that too.

They walked past. The window had not opened yet.

The window opened when Wario and Toad Lee began physically fighting over the paper. Not a verbal dispute — a bodily contest, both of them grabbing the document, Hjumpik pulling at Toad Lee to separate them. In that collision, Wario fell. The papers were momentarily uncontrolled. The room's attention was distributed across the impact.

Waluigi has spent considerable time since asking himself whether he made a decision at that moment or whether the window opened and his body went through it before the decision-making part of his mind had finished forming an opinion. He does not have a satisfying answer. What he knows is that the window existed for approximately two seconds, and he used it.

**Phase 1: The Shuttlecock and the Running**

Waluigi deployed the Phase Spider gut racket — blackened steel frame, Phase Spider gut strings, enchanted to pull kinetic energy from ambient air and manifest it as glowing purple force projectiles. The weapon is illegal in three jurisdictions and two planes. Waluigi uses it for tennis.

He fired. He grabbed what he believed to be the paper. He said 'I need it please.'

Waluigi has analyzed the 'please' at length. It is the word of someone who knows what they are doing is wrong and is asking for permission they have already decided not to wait for. It is not polite. It is the grammatical form of politeness attached to an action that politeness would preclude. Waluigi said it anyway, because certain habits of speech are structural and deploy themselves without conscious authorization.

The shuttlecock caught fire. The enchantment's interaction with ambient fey magic, the force discharge at close range, the general ambient flammability of situations involving Waluigi at five in the morning — the cause is unclear. The result was a burning projectile in Waluigi's hand as he ran.

He ran into Hjumpik.

This is the tactical moment Waluigi considers the actual failure, as opposed to the moral failure of the theft itself. Running into Hjumpik was not strategy. It was not misdirection. It was Waluigi moving faster than he was navigating, in a lounge he did not know well, at five in the morning after several hours of operational activity, with a burning weapon in his hand. The shuttlecock fire damaged Hjumpik. Not Waluigi — Hjumpik. Waluigi's own weapon, caught by Waluigi, used by Waluigi, damaged the person Waluigi ran into.

Hjumpik said: 'Waluigi — after all we've been through.'

Waluigi said: 'I'm sorry. I'll come back. I promise.'

Toad Lee noted there was no promise there. There was trust, which was different. Waluigi was going to be trusted, and what if he was lying. This is a fair tactical assessment of the commitment. Waluigi had said 'I promise' the way a person says it when they mean 'please believe me' and are already moving.

Wario called for the helicopter. Waluigi was running.

**Phase 2: The Pursuit**

Toad Lee pursued. The axe came low — targeting Waluigi's legs rather than anything vital, which Waluigi notes with specific appreciation and documents explicitly. Toad Lee was trying to stop Waluigi, not end him. There is a meaningful distinction between those two objectives and Toad Lee maintained it under conditions where abandoning it would have been understandable.

Waluigi deployed the Cheater's Gambit. Misdirection as competitive strategy. The same underlying principle as Luigi's thunder fake-out, applied in a lounge by a person running from consequences he generated. The gambit exploited the expectation of linear movement — the pursuer's model of where Waluigi was going versus where Waluigi went. It bought momentary mobility. A second axe swing, lower, caught his legs. Waluigi was slowed.

The Cheater's Gambit is not a combat technique. It is a survival technique. There is a difference, and the difference was visible here: Waluigi was not fighting Toad Lee. He was attempting to remain in motion long enough for a situation to resolve itself that he was no longer certain he wanted to resolve the way he had started resolving it.

**Phase 3: Stucky's Eye**

Stucky removed her eye. The milk-white orb — the same eye Waluigi had earlier identified as potentially treatable with mushrooms, bramble juice, and procurable ingredients. She threw it at Waluigi.

She missed. The eye landed on Toad Lee's head.

Waluigi was running and did not see Toad Lee's expression clearly. Based on available evidence, it was the expression of a man who has processed enough in a single morning that a hag's eye landing on his head does not constitute the most statistically anomalous event he has encountered before sunrise. He had reached the point where the unexpected was just additional data.

The eye missed its target. As a projectile, Stucky's throw was inaccurate. As a contribution to the chaos that characterized this engagement, it was fully successful.

**Phase 4: The Ground Pound**

Wario ground-pounded.

Waluigi has seen Wario ground-pound before. The mechanics are not mysterious — Wario leaps, the leap is implausible given his bulk, the descent is faster than physics justifies, the impact in sitting position releases a shockwave that treats nearby structural material as a suggestion rather than a constraint. What is always surprising is the enthusiasm. Wario commits to the ground pound the way he commits to all things that are working correctly: completely, loudly, without reservation.

'WAH HA HA!'

The lounge floor cracked. Spiderwebbing fractures radiated outward from the impact point. Everyone nearby was thrown off their feet or forced to compensate. Stucky almost fell. Hjumpik almost fell. Rakasha Azure did not almost fall — she steadied, absorbed, and then closed her hands around Wario while he was still laughing.

Rakasha caught Wario in an iron grip. He yelled for help.

This is the tactical turning point of the brawl. Not Waluigi being caught. Not Toad Lee's axe. The moment Rakasha physically contained Wario, the commercial logic that had been driving the escalation lost its mobile element. Wario cannot negotiate from a position he cannot exit. Rakasha removed his exit.

**Phase 5: Hjumpik Stops**

Hjumpik deployed what he called his anchor skills.

In tactical terms: he stopped pursuing. He became the fixed point in a room where everything was still moving. He looked at Waluigi and said: 'Come on. It can be another way. It's just money. I don't know you two. There can be another way. Stealing is wrong.'

Waluigi said: 'I think you're right. Why don't we work together as a team?'

Hjumpik said: 'I don't trust you. Give the paper back.'

This is correct tactical doctrine. Hjumpik did not accept Waluigi's reframing. He acknowledged the point being made — yes, another way, yes, working together — and then named the actual operational requirement without allowing the acknowledgment to substitute for the requirement. Give the paper back is not a collaborative proposal. It is a condition. Hjumpik kept it a condition when Waluigi was trying to make it a starting point for negotiation.

Waluigi offered a third party. Hjumpik suggested Stucky, then offered Rakasha. A handoff through Rakasha Azure was arranged.

**Phase 6: What Wario Ate**

Wario, stepping back from Rakasha's grip, asked if anyone liked his Wario bash. Hjumpik said it was alright — Wario had hit him with it, but it was alright. Hjumpik asked Wario to show him the papers. Wario produced a stack.

Then Wario opened his mouth. Impossibly wide. Far wider than anatomy should permit — or rather, far wider than anatomy should permit for someone who is not Wario, which is a category error. For Wario, anatomy is more of a strong suggestion that he honors when convenient.

He chomped. The sound was audible across the room.

Wario ate papers. A stack. He looked at Waluigi afterward.

Only Waluigi saw both the eating and the look. Nobody else's attention was positioned correctly. Everyone else was processing the aftermath of the ground pound, the handoff arrangement, the floor damage, the general operational conclusion of a five AM brawl.

Waluigi is not documenting the full content of the look here. He is documenting that it existed, that it was chosen, that it communicated something that only Waluigi was positioned to receive, and that the papers Wario ate were eaten at a specific moment with the precision Wario applies to all actions involving information he does not want to remain legible.

What Wario ate and why he ate it when he ate it will be addressed in a separate entry when Waluigi has had time to sit with it.

**Resolution: The Handoff and the Floor**

Rakasha confirmed her third-party status. Waluigi handed over the papers. Some turned to dust on contact — she reported this with the calm of someone who has seen magic items deteriorate in wrong-environment exposure and has ceased to find it surprising.

Hjumpik applied a mushroom to himself and felt better. Wario stared at a paper for an uncomfortable duration and gave it back. He said he had clients to see. He left.

Waluigi cried on the floor.

The papers went to Saedia. The debt went nowhere. The kidneys remained attached. The lounge floor remained cracked. The crowned Toad with the Chaos Heart fragment remained unidentified — the most important disclosure of the morning, offered by Wario while he was still being commercially forthcoming, followed up on by nobody with sufficient persistence, including Waluigi, who was thinking about the kidneys instead and documents this as a failure he shares responsibility for.

Wario always walks away. He has calibrated his emotional investment in outcomes to match his capacity for unilateral exit. The result is that Wario never ends up on the floor. He goes to his next appointment.

Waluigi ends up on the floor. He finds this, sitting with it now, both true and not the worst thing about him. The worst thing about him is that he fired first and hit Hjumpik. Everything else is context.

WAH.
aftermath: Papers returned to Saedia. The lounge floor of Ferngrove Manor sustained structural damage from Wario's ground pound that has not been formally assessed. Rakasha Azure confirmed her third-party capabilities under operational conditions. Hjumpik's anchor skills stabilized a situation that was escalating past the point of productive return. Toad Lee maintained lethal/non-lethal discipline under provocation. Stucky's eye was recovered. Wario's commercial interests were not resolved and he departed to pursue them. Waluigi's debt remains outstanding. The crowned Toad buyer of the papers — who paid in a fragment of the Chaos Heart — was not investigated before Wario left the building. Waluigi considers this the most significant tactical failure of the morning, which is notable given that Waluigi also fired a burning shuttlecock at his own teammate.

reputationNotes.waluigi: Fired first but lost; cried on the floor while Wario walked away.

summary: The Greenhouse Reconnaissance was an Iron Legion operation to survey the site of Archie's notorious fireball—the spell that destroyed the Spider Grove's rust monster infestation and established Archie's reputation for collateral damage. Hargram Fidger led a team including Rhak the Lost and Manderaz the Mad to assess remaining threats and document dimensional residue using the Legion Arcane Field Analyzer. What they found was disturbing: the greenhouse still remembered the blast. Combustion echo readings hit 98%. Mirror intrusion readings suggested dimensional bleed. The site's containment risk was rated 'Crimson Alert.' Fae magic had restored the structure's frame but could not erase the violence imprinted on the location. The team eliminated a surviving rust monster, encountered Mages' Guild operatives bagging corpses, and submitted readings that confirmed what Waluigi has long suspected: Archie's magic leaves marks that do not fade. WAH.
description:
Waluigi has reconstructed this operation from Iron Legion field reports and the Legion Arcane Field Analyzer readings that were submitted through official channels. The documentation is remarkably thorough—the Legion takes reconnaissance seriously—allowing Waluigi to understand both what the team found and what it means for the broader crisis.

## The Mission Parameters

Byscilla Danos established the reconnaissance parameters before the team deployed. The greenhouse had been Archie's most documented magical incident—a fireball that destroyed rust monsters, collapsed structures, and generated the Wahwire posts that made Archie's name synonymous with collateral damage.

The Legion wanted to know what remained. Fae magic had apparently restored the greenhouse's frame, but restoration is not erasure. The dimensional instability affecting Raventree Manor might have been amplified by Archie's violent spellcasting. Understanding the site's current state was essential for planning future operations.

The team composition reflected the mission's priorities: Hargram Fidger for tactical leadership, Rhak the Lost for heavy combat capability, Manderaz the Mad for disciplined assessment. No magic users were assigned—they had all been sent to confront Archie directly. This proved significant when combat occurred.

## The Approach — Rain and Rust

The team arrived at the greenhouse during a thunderstorm. Warol the guard briefed them on current conditions: the rust spread faster in rain, Archie had destroyed the main nest, but at least one rust monster remained mobile. Warol had retreated to await reinforcements rather than engage alone.

The greenhouse itself presented a strange sight. The frame had been restored through fae magic—no rust remained on the metal supports, no fire damage marked the structure. But the ground-level evidence told a different story: scorched earth, blackened roots beneath healthy growth, the geological memory of violence that surface restoration could not address.

The team positioned for ambush. The surviving rust monster moved through the greenhouse, apparently unaware of their presence. They waited for optimal positioning.

The rust monster attacked from behind.

## The Engagement — Swift and Efficient

The combat was brief but intense. The rust monster crashed through a former window frame, catching the team off-guard. Manderaz blocked its initial charge. Hargram ordered Rhak to grab it—then reconsidered when Rhak pointed out the risk of his arm rusting.

Rhak swung at the creature's legs. They came off. He followed with a strike to the head. It rolled away.

The rust monster was eliminated in under a minute. The team beheaded it for confirmation, then surveyed the area for additional threats.

A ghost appeared—not from the greenhouse but from the opposite direction. The team dispatched it efficiently, collected the ectoplasm for Guild processing, and resumed their primary mission.

## The Analyzer Readings — What the Site Remembers

The Legion Arcane Field Analyzer provided detailed readings that Waluigi has reproduced in full:

**Combustion Echo: 98%** — The site still remembered the catastrophic blast. Heat memory clung to load-bearing seams and hidden fractures. In Hargram's assessment: 'The blast is gone, but the room still flinches from it.'

**Ferric Hunger: 32%** — Residual rust memory persisted in seams and bolts despite fae restoration. The metal remembered what had consumed it.

**Fae Preservation: 29%** — The restoration magic was active but struggling. Living cover masked older burn trauma below.

**Mirror Intrusion: 68%** — This reading is the most concerning. Dimensional bleed through reflective surfaces suggested the site had become a weak point between planes. Glass, mirrors, and polished water might relay hostile echoes.

**Containment Risk: 77% — CRIMSON ALERT** — The site was rated as high-risk for dimensional instability. Recommendations included reflection discipline before spellcasting, observation rings before deeper exploration, and prohibition on open flame or broad evocation.

The analyzer's interpretation was clear: Archie's fireball had left marks that fae magic could not erase. The greenhouse was a wound in reality that had scabbed over but not healed.

## The Mages' Guild Presence — Bagging the Dead

The reconnaissance team discovered Mages' Guild operatives at the site, bagging rust monster corpses. An individual with an eye patch—possibly a pirate affiliation, possibly criminal underworld connections—was supervising the operation.

The Guild operative approached the Legion team and demanded cooperation. He provided Legion Arcane Field Analyzers for site documentation, explaining that the device sent readings directly to both the Guild and the Legion—a 'joint venture' between organizations.

The interaction suggested that Guild and Legion interests at Raventree Manor were more aligned than either faction publicly acknowledges. Both organizations were documenting Archie's impact on the dimensional environment. Both were preparing for something.

Darno Spriggon arrived later with a letter for Dan and a keychain bearing military insignia. The chain apparently belonged to a general, raising questions about Spriggon's actual rank and authority.

## Waluigi's Analysis — What This Means for Archie

The greenhouse reconnaissance confirms what Waluigi has long suspected: Archie Miser's magic is fundamentally unstable in ways that affect the dimensional environment. His spells do not merely accomplish their immediate purpose—they leave MARKS on reality itself.

A 98% combustion echo fifteen days after the fireball suggests Archie's magic imprints on locations with unusual persistence. Normal spellcasting does not produce readings like this. Archie's casting is different—more violent, more permanent, more disruptive to the dimensional fabric.

The Mages' Guild's interest in Archie makes more sense in this context. They are not merely recruiting a powerful fire mage. They are studying—possibly trying to harness—whatever makes his magic so dimensionally impactful. The 'entropy' that Guild operatives have mentioned in Archie's context may refer to this imprinting effect.

The Legion's interest similarly clarifies. They want to understand and potentially weaponize Archie's dimensional impact. A mage who leaves permanent marks on reality is either an asset to be controlled or a threat to be eliminated. The Legion appears to be pursuing the first option.

Archie himself may not understand what he is. His Wahwire posts suggest he views his magic as conventional fire spellcasting with collateral damage problems. He does not seem to recognize that his magic is fundamentally different from normal casting—that he is not merely powerful but ABERRANT.

The greenhouse reconnaissance documents this aberration in clinical detail. The readings are now in Legion and Guild hands. Both organizations know what Archie is, even if Archie himself does not.

This makes Archie's forced recruitment into the Guild even more concerning. They have not merely drafted a useful mage. They have acquired a dimensional anomaly—one that leaves 98% combustion echoes and 68% mirror intrusion readings wherever he casts.

Waluigi wonders if Archie will ever understand what he is. Waluigi wonders if anyone will tell him.

WAH.

description: The Dream-Duel on the Burning Vigilance is the combat-shaped center of Archie’s nightmare. Original Dan confronts him not with disgust but disdain, and the duel turns into a rules-bound attempt to make guilt measurable. Archie shields, charges, shocks, self-stuns, eats mana bars, rides storm clouds, and stabs Dan, but Dan survives at one hit point and burns him anyway. The repaired Vigilance burning and falling into the sea turns the entire fight into a symbol: the ship can be repaired, but the moral damage is still on fire. Waluigi records this as oneiric combat with strategic psychological value.

summary: A second wave of invisible imps turns the aftermath of the Harvestide 29 cottage siege into a close-quarters tactical engagement. Eager's whip accidentally strikes Salam, Rattles heals and evacuates him, Dan destroys an imp with Divine Smite, and Markop kills two attackers while retaining the Archivist's book. The Toads continue resisting and Markop retains the book; Remi is captured in the confusion and the imps seize the Black Crystal and Mirror. The linked aftermath records Remi's individual capture and later escape from Kyrn's facility; this battle page remains focused on the cottage offensive and its artifact-custody result.
description:
# BATTLE RECORD: THE SECOND IMP OFFENSIVE AT TYMNASS COTTAGE
### Tactical Analysis of the Post-Imp Cottage Defense and Cell Escape
### Filed by Waluigi, Auditor-General of Residential Warfare, Invisible Threats, and Doors That Are Not Locked

This is not a surrender record. Waluigi is correcting the earlier shorthand before it becomes a historical lie. The whole party did not surrender. Markop retained the book, and the Toads continued fighting. Markop kept the Archivist's book. The Toads did not lay down their weapons. The imps took the Black Crystal and Mirror of True Reflection, but they failed to recover the document that brought them to the cottage in the first place.

The engagement has two linked battlefields: a cottage with broken sightlines and a holding facility with broken security. The first battlefield is won by the defenders in the narrow sense that Markop disburses the remaining imps and keeps the book. The second is won by Remi in the narrow sense that she escapes with Mossy. The strategic situation is still bad: the imps leave with two portal artifacts, Salam is unconscious, and Kyrn has demonstrated that a damaged cell can still be used to destroy a friend.

## 1. Operational Clock

**29 Harvestide, dawn:** the first Imp Ambush begins at Tymnas's Cottage.

**29 Harvestide, shortly after dawn:** the second offensive begins. Eager's whip strikes Salam; Tymnas is stung; Remi blocks an attack; additional imps enter the rear room.

**29 Harvestide, later in the same crisis:** Rattles heals the defenders, Salam is evacuated, Dan smites an imp, Markop kills two attackers, and Markop retains the book while the Toads continue resisting.

**29–30 Harvestide, exact cell hour unknown:** Remi is captured, encounters Kyrn, watches Mossy melt, escapes the unlocked cell, repairs the construct, and exits with it. Shadowfell time does not provide a trustworthy minute reading.

## 2. Force Composition and Objectives

The imp force is a retrieval cell, not a conventional army. Its objective is narrow: recover the Archivist's book and remove the people obstructing that recovery. The right-hand man provides coordination, while subordinate imps use invisibility, flanking, stings, and attacks through the rear room.

The defenders have no single commander in the second phase. Markop holds the book and directs the practical defense. Dan identifies and destroys a threat with a divine smite. Rattles supplies healing and evacuation. Remi uses a shield and silent musket. Tymnas fights after being stung. Eager uses a whip and pepper spray while trying not to become another casualty. Salam is both combatant and casualty when Eager's strike lands incorrectly.

The asymmetry is immediate. The imps know their objective. The defenders know only that the cottage is filling with invisible bodies. The defenders' first tactical priority should be shared target acquisition. Instead, each person receives a separate attack and answers locally.

## 3. Friendly-Fire Failure

Eager's whip is aimed at a ripple near the pantry. The target is not confirmed. The strike misses the imp and hits Salam in the head. Salam collapses. This is not a moral failure and not a reason to remove Eager from the line; it is a target-identification failure produced by invisible enemies and a crowded room.

The correction is simple but expensive: no blind melee swing without a callout, a visible disturbance, or a defensive purpose. Dan's eye and Rattles's healing later demonstrate the correct method. The party needs a sensor, a caller, and a designated strike window. Before that happens, the room pays for the missing system with Salam's consciousness.

## 4. Rear-Room Breach

While the front line absorbs pressure, more imps storm Remi's room. This is the attacker's decisive maneuver. The cottage defenders treat the front door as the battle. The imps treat the washroom window as the route around the battle.

Remi blocks an attack with her shield, moves down from another attacker, and fires the silent musket into an imp's face. Her silence matters tactically: the shot does not reveal her position to every enemy in the building. The rear room remains a contested space instead of becoming a beacon.

Tymnas swings at an invisible attacker and connects. The hit makes the imp visible for an instant. This reveals a practical counter: damage is not merely damage; it is a temporary identification tool. Every successful strike should be called out, followed, and used to relocate the target before it vanishes.

## 5. Collapse of the Salam Position

Salam runs. He jumps over Dan and collides with an imp that reveals itself on contact. He falls again. Eager asks whether Salam does anything at all. Rattles answers not with an argument but with healing.

Rattles' healing wave restores the group enough to continue, but Salam remains in danger. Rattles chooses evacuation. He picks Salam up and throws him through the broken window. This is not abandonment. It is casualty removal: take the wounded body out of the kill zone before the room turns the casualty into a second enemy flank.

The window creates a third battlefield below the cottage. Salam is no longer available for coordinated strikes, but he is also no longer available to the imps. The decision preserves the possibility of recovery.

## 6. Dan's Radiant Counterstrike and Markop's Axe

An imp stings Dan. Dan answers with Divine Smite. The radiant strike forces the imp visible, drives it into the wall, and leaves a black mark in the plaster. The smite does three jobs: damage, identification, and morale. It tells the defenders that the invisible force can be made to occupy physical space.

Rattles evacuates Salam while Markop swings twice. Markop kills two imps at the turning point. The important fact is not simply the number of dead attackers. It is what Markop does with the opening: he retains the book and disburses the remaining imps rather than accepting the attackers' demand.

The imp force came for the book. It leaves without it.

## 7. Artifact Loss Without Book Loss

The imp force does successfully seize the Black Crystal and Mirror of True Reflection. These are portal artifacts, and losing them is strategically serious. They are not the same object as the Archivist's book.

The book remains with Markop. This distinction changes the next operation. The imps have two pieces of the portal chain, but they do not have the document that may explain the cell, the planes, or the relationships between the objects. Markop's retention is a tactical success even though the party loses artifacts and Remi.

Waluigi's earlier Shadow Estate artifact records established that the Black Crystal, Mirror, Umbral Signet, and Orb of Shadow Domination are distributed across a chain of events. This battle adds a new distribution state: the imps hold two artifacts, the party holds the book, and the holding facility holds the people who know how the objects were used.

## 8. Capture of Remi

The defenders do not surrender as a whole. Remi is captured in the confusion while the cottage defense fragments. This is an individual capture inside a continuing battle, not a party capitulation.

That distinction matters to the tactical record. Markop and the Toads continue resisting. The book remains in their possession. Remi is moved to the facility because the imps exploit the separation created by the rear-room breach and the defenders' casualty evacuation.

The imps therefore win a person and two artifacts, but fail the primary retrieval objective. This is a mixed tactical result, not a clean victory.

## 9. Post-Battle Consequences

The battle page ends when the cottage line is decided. Remi's later capture, Kyrn's ray, Mossy's repair, and the unlocked-cell escape belong to the linked aftermath event, not the core imp battle. They matter because they are the consequences of the imp offensive, but they are a different battlefield with different objectives.

The cottage result is therefore precise: Markop keeps the book, the Toads continue fighting, and the remaining imps are disbursed. The attackers leave with the Black Crystal and Mirror of True Reflection. Remi's individual capture is the cost of the rear-room breach; it is not a whole-party surrender.

## 11. Result

**Cottage result:** Markop retains the Archivist's book and disburses the remaining imps. Salam is evacuated unconscious. The Toads do not surrender as a whole; Remi is captured during the confusion.

**Artifact result:** The imp force takes the Black Crystal and Mirror of True Reflection.

**Prison result:** Remi escapes at one hit point and repairs Mossy. Gregir also escapes. The facility remains active and contains other prisoners.

**Strategic result:** Neither side receives everything it wants. The imps gain two portal artifacts and a temporary capture. The defenders retain the book and gain a route into Kyrn's facility.

*Waluigi's final tactical note: the imps came for a book and left carrying a mirror. Markop kept the pages. Remi kept the dog. The Toads kept fighting. This is not a surrender. This is a battle that changed owners for two objects and changed rooms for everyone else. WAH.*
